label: PF Backlog 432
title: B2: gateways (Model/Tool/Memory/Infrastructure)

analysis.implementation_strategy: Introduce four thin gateway interfaces (ModelGateway, ToolGateway, MemoryGateway, InfrastructureGateway) in core, then route existing call sites through them. Reuse current assets as the first adapters: model routing/policy from core/agent_model_override.py + conversation_models.py + config/model-catalog.json + model-policy.json + model-tier.json; tools from core/agent_tool_loop.py + /api/v1/tools/catalog + config/tool-catalog.json; memory from core/agent_memory.py; infrastructure from core/deploy_providers.py + /api/v1/engineering/worker-providers. Keep config JSON as the gateway config format; do not rewrite adapters in Go yet (per BI-PF-0387 migrate-by-value policy).
conflict_findings: Touches core/agent_tool_loop.py and core/agent_memory.py which BI-PF-0405/BI-PF-0406 may also modify - serialize or assign clear ownership per module.
Config catalog JSON files are shared - changes to schema must land before parallel config consumers.
duplication_findings: core/agent_model_override.py + config/model-catalog/policy/tier.json already implement de-facto model routing - ModelGateway should wrap these, not replace them.
core/agent_tool_loop.py + /api/v1/tools/catalog already implement tool discovery/execution - ToolGateway wraps these.
BI-PF-0406 (service decomposition) will re-expose these gateways across process boundaries - coordinate so gateway interfaces are transport-agnostic.
BI-PF-0405 (WASM plugins) will likely hook into ToolGateway - the interface must allow plugin registration without core edits.
BI-PF-0414 pluggable store covers persistence and must NOT be re-implemented inside MemoryGateway.
analysis.rationale: Provider coupling already hurts and the codebase has clear seams: model override, tool loop, memory and deploy providers modules plus their config catalogs. Reuse-first: define gateway interfaces and wrap the existing modules as adapters; no new provider logic is written.
assumptions: Existing modules already concentrate provider interactions behind few call sites.
Gateway config can remain JSON catalogs initially.
Per BI-PF-0387 new sensitive logic goes to Go - gateways may start in Python and be migrated by value.
WorkerGrid/B2 infra gateway must satisfy both single-node and multi-node deployments.
risks: Over-abstraction: building generic gateway framework before real multi-provider demand materializes.
Provider coupling may be deeper than the visible call sites (hidden direct SDK calls).
Streaming/async semantics of model calls may not fit a simple sync interface.
Edition gating (which gateways exist per edition) is undefined.
evidence: Candidate modules and config catalogs listed for this item
BI-PF-0387 compiled-only baseline constrains where new gateway code may live
BI-PF-0406/BI-PF-0405 titles indicate later reuse of these interfaces
missing_info: Gateway interface contract: sync vs async, streaming support, error taxonomy.
Which provider integrations are must-have for the first slice (OpenAI, Anthropic, local?).
Edition matrix: which gateways ship in which edition.
Whether gateways stay Python (compiled) or move to Go core now.
Config schema versioning approach for the catalogs.

context_review.reason: All four domains already have concrete modules and config catalogs to wrap; implementation is interface-first refactoring. Human must fix the interface contract and edition matrix before coding.

brief.problem: Core modules import concrete providers, coupling PF to them; swapping a provider requires code changes.
brief.what_adds: B2 — gateways for Model / Tool / Memory / Infrastructure so core depends on ports, not concrete providers.
brief.why: Decouple core from providers; swap via config only. Trigger: provider coupling hurts.
brief.who_feels: PF platform maintainers, workers, and customers.

objective: B2 — gateways for Model / Tool / Memory / Infrastructure so core depends on ports, not concrete providers.
acceptance_criteria: no core module imports a concrete provider
a provider is swapped via config only
approach: Define core gateway ports; route all provider access through them; select the provider via config; forbid core importing a concrete provider (fail closed).
